column1: # tools/doom/core-builtin-effects.tsv — what a builtin call does to its receiver,
# The setup walk records every field Full's setup writes before the first tick,
# and a stored field it does not list keeps its allocation fill. A call with no
# tree definition runs no tree code, but that is not evidence it writes nothing:
# `@a.fill(7)` rewrites @a. So every builtin the walk reaches must be listed
# here, by name and receiver type, as one of:
#   pure       reads its receiver and arguments; changes neither
#   mutates    changes its receiver, which the walk then attributes to the
#              field that receiver is (or refuses, as a gap, when it cannot say)
#   control    no receiver to change (`raise`, `loop`); a block's body is walked
#              as the enclosing definition's own code
# A call whose name and receiver type match no row is a GAP, named, and the
# emitter will not use a walk that has one. This is not tools/doom/core-builtins.tsv:
# that says whether CORE may call a builtin; this says what the call changes.
# `*` as the receiver matches any receiver type.
